title: It doesn’t make sense at first.
paragraphs: It doesn’t make sense at first.

A righteous man…
Blameless. Upright. God-fearing.

So the question hits hard:
Why would God allow Satan to test Job?
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

This wasn’t random suffering.
This was a courtroom.
Before the pain ever touched Job, there was a conversation in heaven.
“Then the LORD said to Satan, ‘Have you considered My servant Job, that there is none like him on the earth…?’” — Job 1:8

Not because He wanted to destroy him…
But because He trusted him.
And Satan responds with an accusation that still echoes today:
“Does Job fear God for nothing? … Stretch out Your hand and touch all that he has, and he will surely curse You to Your face.” — Job 1:9–11

Not Job’s comfort.
Not his possessions.
“People only love God when life is good.”

And if that’s true… then worship is fake.
Faith is conditional.
And God is not truly worthy—just useful.

Not to harm Job.
But to silence the lie.
“Behold, all that he has is in your power. Only do not lay a hand on his person.” — Job 1:12
“Behold, he is in your hand, but spare his life.” — Job 2:6

Satan is not equal to God.
He is on a leash.

Every trial had a limit.
Every attack had a boundary.
God remained sovereign the entire time.
And in the silence of grief, this is what he says:
“The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.” — Job 1:21
This is where most people walk away.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
Job’s story is not ultimately about suffering.

That God is worthy—
not because of what He gives,
but because of who He is.
And this points forward to something greater.
“For I know that my Redeemer lives, and He shall stand at last on the earth.” — Job 19:25
He didn’t even fully understand it.
But he was pointing to Jesus Christ.
You and I are not like Job.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
“But God demonstrates His own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
Total loss. Total suffering. Total separation.
So you wouldn’t have to face God’s wrath.
Why did God allow Satan to test Job?

• To expose the lie that faith is conditional
• To demonstrate that God is worthy beyond blessing
• To reveal His sovereignty over evil
• To foreshadow a greater redemption through Christ
Because your life will be tested too.
Do you love God… or just what He gives?
This Is Where It Turns Personal
If this found you, it’s not by accident.
There are things happening in your life right now you don’t understand.
And you’re asking the same question Job did:
There’s More You Haven’t Seen Yet

• Spiritual warfare you didn’t know was happening
• How God uses suffering to refine—not destroy
• How to stand when everything collapses
• The unseen battle over your soul
And you’re being invited into the same.

Turn from sin.
Trust in Jesus Christ.
“Come to Me, all you who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.” — Matthew 11:28

If you want to go deeper—
real depth, not surface-level faith—
If this stirred something in you:
Because the battle isn’t just around you.
